extracted.intended_audience: issuers preparing initial registration statements, SEC reporting/accounting teams, IPO advisors and securities lawyers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on which pre-acquisition and pro forma financial statements must be included in an initial registration statement (IPO or first-time registrant), how to identify and test acquired businesses for significance under S-X Rule 3-05, and related presentation and relief considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of S-X Rule 3-05 in initial registration statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, financial statements of an acquired business are included in an initial registration statement to comply with S-X Rule 3-05; those financial statements must comply in form and content with S-X Rule 3-05.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter addresses unique issues for initial registration statements (determining significance of acquisitions, time periods for evaluation, put-together transactions, combinations under common control, and SAB 80 relief). Include pre-acquisition financial statements when acquisition meets applicable significance thresholds; follow S-X Rule 3-05 format and content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which acquisitions to test for significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform significance tests for all acquisitions since the earliest year for which audited financial statements are required to be filed in the initial registration statement (i.e., within the last two or three years depending on filer status).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-acquisition financials can be omitted if acquiree operations have been included in the registrant’s post-acquisition audited consolidated results for a sufficient period (see omission thresholds). In addition to consummated historical acquisitions, assess probable acquisitions that exceed 50% significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission thresholds based on period of post-acquisition results
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant may omit audited pre-acquisition financial statements if the acquiree’s operations have been included in the registrant’s audited consolidated financial statements for a sufficient period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible omissions: one full year (12 months) of inclusion permits omission regardless of significance; nine months of inclusion may permit omission only if acquisition significance exceeds 20% but is not 40% or greater. Examples illustrate when two years, one year, and interim statements are required based on months included and significance percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance tests (reference to chapter 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance of an acquisition is determined using the significance tests described in chapter 3 of the Handbook (asset, investment, and income tests as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the numerical significance tests from chapter 3 to decide whether to include pre-acquisition financial statements and for how many years. Examples show asset-test and income-test calculations and resulting significance percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required financial-statement period to determine significance (no choice)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an initial registration statement, a registrant is required to perform the significance tests using the most recent pre-acquisition audited financial statements required to be filed on the initial registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC staff view is that registrants do not have a choice to use an alternate fiscal period; use the most recent pre-acquisition audited year-end included in the registration statement. [Regs Comm 03/2021]

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of later year financials in draft/confidential filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A company that confidentially submits draft registration statements may determine significance using the most recent year-end audited financial statements even if those statements are not included in the draft, provided those audited statements will be included in the first public filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEC staff encourages companies to notify the Division of Corporation Finance of the circumstances before confidential submission. [Regs Comm 03/2018] This relief is tied to confidential draft review and the expectation that later audited statements will be in the first public filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of filed pro forma financial information to determine significance
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant can determine significance using filed pro forma financial information that depicts acquisitions consummated after the latest fiscal year-end if certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: (1) audited Rule 3-05 (or Rule 3-14) financial statements for any such acquired business have been (or will be) included; and (2) the pro forma financial information required by S-X Article 11 for the acquired/disposed businesses will be included. Pro forma information used in draft registration statements is appropriate only if it will be included in the final filed initial registration statement. [SEC Rel 33-10786 FN 196; Regs Comm 09/2021]

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pro forma to determine significance when change in control has occurred
rubrics_metrics.description: When a registrant is a successor to a predecessor (change in control), the successor’s results are used in the denominator of the income test if a full-year successor statement is not available; use of pro forma may be permitted with SEC staff permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using only successor-period results yields anomalous results, the registrant may request permission from the SEC staff to use pro forma amounts as if the predecessor had been acquired (or change in control occurred) at the fiscal year start. Draft examples show when written requests are necessary. [Regs Comm 09/2021; FRM 2025.10]

rubrics_metrics.name: Probable acquisitions requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Probable acquisitions (not yet consummated) that exceed 50% significance must be assessed and may require inclusion of financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants should assess not only consummated acquisitions but also probable acquisitions that meet the 50% threshold when preparing an initial registration statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAST Act / EGC relief to omit certain financial information
rubrics_metrics.description: An emerging growth company (EGC) filing (or submitting for confidential review) an IPO registration statement can omit historical financial information it reasonably believes will not be required at the time of the contemplated offering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relief can include Rule 3-05 financial statements that an EGC would otherwise be required to provide. Non-EGC registrants do not receive FAST Act omission relief and must conform to applicable rules and forms on the initial filing date. [§71003 FAST Act; SEC Corp Fin Announcement]

rubrics_metrics.name: Put-together transactions — identify accounting acquirer and group related businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: In put-together transactions (Newco/shell formed to acquire multiple unrelated businesses concurrently with an IPO), identify the accounting acquirer and test significance of all acquired businesses against that acquirer because they are treated as related.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All acquired businesses in the put-together are considered related and grouped and assessed for significance against the accounting acquirer as a single acquisition. The accounting acquirer may be different from the registrant. SEC staff may grant relief from literal application of S-X Rule 3-05 on written request. [FRM 2025.12]

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statements used to determine significance after a put-together transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: If a new acquisition occurs after an IPO that involved a put-together transaction but before the new registrant’s first Form 10-K, significance is measured against the audited financial statements of the accounting acquirer for the most recent fiscal year included in the IPO registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the acquisition takes place after the filing of the registrant’s first Form 10-K, measure significance against the registrant’s audited financial statements for the most recent fiscal year in the Form 10-K. SEC staff may consider relief depending on timing relative to the balance sheet date. [FRM 2025.13]

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of financial statements for combinations of entities under common control
rubrics_metrics.description: How to reflect combinations of entities under common control in an initial registration statement depends on timing: combinations during historical periods are reflected in historical F/S; combinations occurring on/after effectiveness but before closing are presented separately unless SEC permits combined/consolidated as primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the combination occurs during presented historical periods, reflect in those statements. If the combination will occur when or after the registration statement becomes effective but no later than IPO closing, present separate financials of the registrant and reorganized entities; SEC staff may allow consolidated/combined financial statements as the primary presentation on request. If merger occurs after IPO closing, reflect in pro forma financial information for the same periods as historical F/S. [FRM 13410.3]

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining significance when historical statements are updated for common-control combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: When prior-period financial statements have been retrospectively adjusted using the as-if pooling-of-interests method for entities under common control, significance of prior acquisitions is determined using the registrant’s as-if pooled (restated) financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers among entities under common control are generally accounted for at historical cost (as-if pooling-of-interests); use the retrospectively adjusted combined amounts for the same periods presented to calculate significance for acquisitions that occurred prior to the legal consummation of the combination. SEC staff may consider relief to use combined amounts when the change in reporting entity occurs on or after effectiveness but before IPO closing. [FRM 2015.2]

rubrics_metrics.name: Which financial statements are required for combinations under common control (parent/predecessor determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine required financial statements, first identify the parent entity and then determine the predecessor; the predecessor provides full financial statements as a registrant would (S-X 3-01/3-02 or 8-02/8-03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The predecessor is typically the entity first controlled by the parent. No parent financial statements are required in the registration statement, but the parent determination affects accounting in combined financial statements. The predecessor is not eligible for any relief that may be available under S-X Rule 3-05 for an acquired business. [FRM 1170]

rubrics_metrics.name: SAB 80 — application and staff rationale for relief
rubrics_metrics.description: SAB Topic 1.J (SAB 80) discusses application of Rule 3-05 and Rule 1-02(w) for initial public offerings and recognizes that literal application may require financial statements for acquirees that are not meaningful to investors because the registrant has grown substantially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules 3-05 and 1-02(w) calculations use financial data for the fiscal years most recently completed prior to the acquisition. SAB 80 provides interpretive guidance and staff rationale addressing situations where strict application may produce results that are not investor-relevant, supporting requests for relief in appropriate circumstances.
